title: Cold rebuild: Model cherry-pick
summary: Rebuild Model cherry-pick from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Model cherry-pick** in *Cherry-pick, and merge vs rebase*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: After `git cherry-pick F`, is the new commit F' the same commit as F?
options: No: same change and message, but a different parent, so a different hash
Yes, if there were no conflicts
steps.explain: That is why later merging both branches is fine (Git sees the same change twice and it merges cleanly) but `git log` shows two commits with the same message.

steps.title: Backport one fix, cold
prompt: `~/shop`: the commit `Fix VAT rounding` on `main` must go to `release/2.4` as well, and nothing else from `main` may come with it.
Copy it so the message says which commit it came from. Leave `main` as it is. From memory: no hints this time.
